newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Norilsk drags leading shares down - traders.
newsitem.headline: Russia Norilsk drags leading shares down - traders.

text.p: News of troubled finances at Russian metals producer Norilsk Nickel helped drag leading Russian shares down in early trading on Monday, traders said.
They predicted the market would close lower as operators on the London and New York stock exchanges observe market holidays.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened slightly up at 356.41 after 356.27 on Friday, but traders forecast a fall by the end of the day.
"It was very negative news about Nickel and that played a role (in driving the market down)," said Rossiisky Kredit Bank trader Alexander Zyuzlikov.

Norilsk, one of the world's most significant producers of nickel, platinum group metals and cobalt, said last Friday that it had a consolidated 3.29 trillion rouble ($571.9 million) loss for 1996. Norilsk said in a statement it was showing signs of bankruptcy, requiring radical steps in the next six months.
It had risen strongly last week on plans to issue American Depositary Receipts soon to allow foreign trade, but said on Monday the issue may be delayed.
Norilsk Nickel plunged to $6.390 at 0820 GMT from $7.330 on Friday but recovered to $6.620 by 0850 GMT.
Traders said the morning fall was also a correction to the market's rise in the previous week.
A trader at a Western brokerage also said market holidays in the West would keep activity and prices low on the Russian market.
"It will be very quiet today because of the holiday in London and New York," he said. "The market opened rather flabby and down and I don't expect any particular jumps today."
National electricity company UES fell back to $0.3170 from the $0.3219 level it achieved on Friday on news company chief executive Anatoly Dyakov would be replaced by vice-president Boris Brevnov.
Oil producer Tatneft registered the highest turnover at 0920 GMT with $5.26 million.

Sergei Dyuden, head of trading operations at Solid, a Tatneft market maker, said investors were snapping up shares from profit-takers ahead of an expected decision at the Tatneft shareholders meeting in June to split shares 100 to one.
"The (split) process is good news... and should lead to future growth," said Dyuden, noting that Tatneft, at $85.000, was currently around all-time high levels.
"We're seeing the intersection of the desires of sellers and the demand which has appeared on the announcement (of the share split)."
Natural gas group Gazprom, which showed the market's highest turnover on Friday, about $31 million to UES's $14 million, fell to $0.647 after rising to an early $0.665 from $0.655 on Friday.
